items.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: George was a good enough arranger... I learned a lot about technique, just from playing his music... when you were in the band

ctx.x: Yeah, we’ve been, we were in this country for probably, oh God, six, seven, eight generations. And before that England. And my mother, my uncle, my uncle George was a composer, he was, he wrote shows, reviews and all that sort of thing. Music and lyrics, and he was very talented but never made it in this country. He had success in England in the mid-30s but World War two scared him back here. And when he grew up, he was growing up in Chicago he was part of the Austin High School gang, you know with Bud Freeman;…
What are your earliest musical memories?
